name: Hydroxypropyl methylcellulose
description: Hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (CAS 9004-65-3 ), commercially known as HPMC and approved as food additive E464 , is a cellulose-derived polymer used across pharmaceuticals, construction, food, and personal care. It functions primarily as a thickener, binder, and film-former, controlling viscosity and water retention in a broad range of formulations. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, HPMC is a critical excipient for tablet coating. It is used for controlled-release matrix systems and capsule shells, including vegetarian alternatives to gelatin. Tile adhesives, cement renders, and dry-mix mortars rely on it to extend open time. This material improves workability on construction sites. Food manufacturers use E464 to stabilize emulsions, control texture in low-fat products, and prevent moisture migration in baked goods. In personal care, it thickens shampoos, gels, and ophthalmic solutions while providing a smooth, non-tacky film on skin and hair. HPMC is supplied as a white to off-white powder in a range of viscosity grades. It is typically characterized by methoxy and hydroxypropoxy substitution levels. Established grades include USP /NF, Ph.Eur. , BP , and food-grade ( FCC /E464-compliant) specifications to meet regulatory requirements. These standards ensure safety across various global industries. Technical-grade material is also available for construction applications where pharmaceutical or food compliance is not required.
